subject: humanities
passage: During Japan's Edo period, the shakuhachi, an end-blown flute cut from the root end of a bamboo stalk, was closely associated with the komuso, wandering monks of a Zen sect who treated playing the instrument as a form of meditation. Several features set these monks apart from other ______ the deep basket hat, woven from reeds, that covered the face entirely and signaled the wearer's withdrawal from the world; the long solo pieces, passed down from teacher to student, that they played while walking from house to house; and the bowl into which listeners dropped coins or rice. After the sect was abolished in 1871, the pieces survived among secular players.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

explanation.why: "Several features set these monks apart from other travelers" is an independent clause, and what follows is the list of those features, with semicolons separating items that contain commas. A colon after an independent clause introduces such a list.
explanation.A: Incorrect. A semicolon must have an independent clause after it, but "the deep basket hat, woven from reeds, that covered the face …" is a noun phrase, not a clause.
explanation.B: Correct. The colon follows a complete clause and introduces the list of features that the clause promises.
explanation.C: Incorrect. A comma would make "the deep basket hat" read as a description of "other travelers" rather than the first item of a list.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Without any mark, "other travelers the deep basket hat" runs the clause into the list it introduces.
